:::{#def-armijo-condition}
#### Armijo condition

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ have first partial derivatives,
let $\vx \in \reals^p$, and let $\vecf{g} \eqdef \deriv{\vx} f(\vx)$.
A step length $s > 0$ satisfies the **Armijo condition**
[@wikipedia_backtracking_line_search]
with constant $c \in (0, 1)$ at $\vx$ if

$$
f(\vx - s \vecf{g}) \le f(\vx) - c\, s\, \norm{\vecf{g}}^2.
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-armijo-condition}
#### The Armijo condition on a parabola

Let $f(x) = x^2$ and $x = 2$, so $g = f'(2) = 4$ and $\norm{g}^2 = 16$.
With $c = 1/4$, the condition on a step length $s > 0$ is

$$
\ba
(2 - 4s)^2 &\le 4 - 4s
&& \text{(} f(2 - 4s) \le f(2) - c\, s\, \norm{g}^2 \text{)}
\\
4 - 16 s + 16 s^2 &\le 4 - 4s
&& \text{(expand the square)}
\\
16 s^2 &\le 12 s
&& \text{(add } 16 s - 4 \text{ to both sides)}
\\
s &\le 3/4.
&& \text{(divide by } 16 s > 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

So $s = 1/2$ satisfies the condition: $f(0) = 0 \le 4 - 2 = 2$.
And $s = 1$ does not: $f(-2) = 4 > 4 - 4 = 0$.

:::
